draft.title: Confidence intervals for a mean
card: An approximate 95% confidence interval for the population mean μ is x̄ ± 1.96 × σ/√n. Here x̄ is the sample mean, σ is the population standard deviation and n is the sample size.
Example: x̄ = 50, σ = 10, n = 100. Then σ/√n = 10/10 = 1, so the margin is 1.96 × 1 = 1.96. The interval is 48.04 to 51.96.
The 95% describes the method. If we took many samples and built an interval from each, about 95% of those intervals would contain μ.
A larger n gives a smaller margin, because n is under a square root. Four times the sample size halves the margin.
draft.remember: Interval = sample mean ± 1.96 × σ/√n. A bigger sample gives a narrower interval.

a.q: Mia weighs 64 packets of rice and finds a mean of 200 g. The population standard deviation is 16 g. What is the approximate 95% interval for μ?
a.why: σ/√n = 16/8 = 2, so the margin is 1.96 × 2 = 3.92. The interval is 200 ± 3.92. The wide interval 168.64 to 231.36 comes from forgetting to divide by √n.
a.clue: Divide σ by the square root of 64 before multiplying.

b.q: A 95% interval for a mean has a margin of 4.0 from a sample of 25. A new sample of 100 is taken from the same population, with the same σ. What is the approximate new margin?
b.why: The sample size is four times larger and √4 = 2, so the margin is halved to about 2.0. A margin of 1.0 comes from dividing by 4 instead of by √4.
b.clue: The margin changes with √n, not with n.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: the interval is 200 ± 3.92, and quadrupling n halves the margin to about 2.0.
